claims.text: Local chemical order in high-entropy alloys enhances corrosion resistance.
Local chemical order reduces the formation of irradiation-induced defects.
Reducing irradiation-induced defects inhibits corrosion initiation.
Reducing irradiation-induced defects inhibits corrosion propagation.
Tailoring local chemical order in HEAs will improve corrosion resistance relative to alloys without tailored local chemical order.
The proposed mechanism applies under chemical-processing operating conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies under nuclear-power operating conditions.
Local chemical order can be introduced through advanced characterization and processing techniques.
Atom probe tomography and electron nanodiffraction can be used to investigate local chemical order in HEAs.
Corrosion rate, defect density, and local chemical order parameters are the proposed measurable responses.
Failure to find a significant correlation between local chemical order and corrosion resistance would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of introduced local chemical order to improve corrosion resistance would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The target material shifts from steels and conventional-steel baselines to unspecified HEAs. The hypothesis does not establish that the tested HEAs are steels or compositionally matched to the baseline, so the stated material system is internally inconsistent and potentially confounded.

The intervention says local chemical order is introduced through characterization and processing, whereas the experiment only describes characterization to investigate order and supplies no processing operation that actually manipulates it.
